To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) B. napus is able to forage in patchy water supplies, (ii) root foraging was more effective than alternate watering in the first greenhouse experiment, but less effective in the second field experiment with larger plants, (iii) alternate watering was more effective than uniform watering in the field experiment with larger plant size, but less effective than uniform watering with smaller plants in the first greenhouse pot experiment, and (iv) root foraging and alternate watering are not equally effective in

partial root drying (PR D) is an effective way to stimulate root growth and foraging, and thus improve biomass production, but the effectiveness depends on the water supply level, the plant developmental stage and the plant species.

Root foraging for patchily distributed soil moisture was not effective in improving the growth of oilseed rape under water deficiency, and the effects of alternate watering on shoot biomass were not related to stomatal conductance but depended on the severity of water stress and on the time of harvesting."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how root placement and water-use efficiency affect plant growth under water stress and the potential of PRD to improve crop production under water scarcity.
how plants respond to partial root drying and whether this response is useful for improving plant growth and yield under water stress.
the mechanisms underlying PRD effects and how these mechanisms may be affected by the environment and the growth stage of the plant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PRD can increase biomass production of oilseed rape, but the success depends on the water supply level and the time of harvest.
partial root drying can improve plant water status and growth, but only when the water is not too patchily distributed and the plants are not too large.
PRD effects on plant growth depend on the plant species, plant developmental stage and water supply level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the partial root drying effects on biomass production depend on the water supply level and on plant growth stage.
partial root drying can increase biomass production in oilseed rape under water deficiency, but the effect is not as strong as previously reported for other crops.
partial root drying can be a useful strategy for improving crop growth and biomass production, and that the root system is capable of responding to patchy water supply.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the root responses to partial root drying may be more important than previously assumed.
the effects of partial root zone drying on biomass production depend on the plant growth stage, the water supply level and the water supply pattern.
root responses to partial root drying are complex and may depend on the plant species and the experimental conditions, and thus should be considered in future studies.
